dublinCore.title: Sine Wave
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Sine waves
Sinusoidal signals
Amplitude
Period and frequency
Phase
dublinCore.description: Interactive plot of y(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) over a 10 ms window. Amplitude, period and phase sliders change the wave, with markers for A, T and the time shift and read-outs of frequency and angular frequency.
relation: Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Identify the amplitude, period and phase of a sine wave from the markers on its plot
Calculate the frequency f = 1/T and the angular frequency ω = 2πf from a period read off the time axis
Predict how changing the amplitude, period or phase alters the plotted wave before moving a slider
Compute the time shift Δt = −φT/2π produced by a given phase and explain why it depends on the period
Explain why a phase of +90° turns a sine wave into a cosine wave
prerequisites: Graphing a function on a Cartesian grid

misconceptions.misconception: Phase is a time delay measured in milliseconds, and a positive phase moves the wave to the right
misconceptions.correction: Phase is an angle, a fraction of one cycle, so the same phase gives a different time shift for each period; in A sin(ωt + φ) a positive phase moves the wave left
misconceptions.evidence: Set φ = 90° and compare the time-shift arrow at T = 2.0 ms (Δt = −0.50 ms) and T = 4.0 ms (Δt = −1.00 ms)

misconceptions.misconception: A longer period means a higher frequency
misconceptions.correction: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period, f = 1/T, so a longer period means a lower frequency
misconceptions.evidence: Increase T from 2.0 ms to 4.0 ms and watch f fall from 500.0 Hz to 250.0 Hz while the window holds fewer cycles

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Plot of a sine wave over a 10 millisecond window. Three sliders set the amplitude A from 0 to 2, the period T from 0.5 to 5 milliseconds and the phase from minus 180 to plus 180 degrees. A read-out panel gives the equation, the frequency, the angular frequency, the time shift and the value at time zero.

controls.label: Amplitude A
controls.description: Sets the peak value of the sine wave in arbitrary units

controls.label: Period T (ms)
controls.description: Sets the time of one full cycle in milliseconds; the frequency read-out is 1000/T in hertz

controls.label: Phase φ (degrees)
controls.description: Sets the phase angle of the sine wave; a positive phase moves the wave to the left

visualElements.description: Time-domain plot of the sine wave in blue with a one-millisecond grid, dashed lines at plus and minus A, a dimension line one period wide and a time-shift arrow
Read-out panel with the equation, f = 1/T, angular frequency, time shift and y(0)

model.description: Evaluates y(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi) once per pixel across the -5 ms to +5 ms window and derives f, omega and the time shift from T and phi
equations: y(t) = A sin(2 pi t / T + phi)

instructionalStrategies: Vary one parameter at a time and observe what stays fixed
Predict-then-verify the time shift for a given phase and period
extensions: Add the cosine and tangent functions to the plot
Add a second sinusoid and show the sum of two waves
